'''Enomiya Shrine''' (宅宮神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社}} located in {{ill|Tokushima (city)|ja|徳島市}}, Kamiyachiman Town, Tokushima Prefecture, Japan.

== History ==
The shrine's founding date is unknown. It is identified with the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyocho|ja|延喜式神名帳}}'' entry for {{ill|Otoma Hime Shrine|ja|意富門麻比売神社}} in {{ill|Awa Province|ja|阿波国}}, Namikata District ({{ill|Shikinai Shrine|ja|式内社}}). It is the only shrine enshrining {{ill|Otonoji and Otonobe|ja|大苫辺尊|lt=Otomabe no Mikoto}}, making it notable among the Namikata District's 12 shrines. In 874 ({{ill|Jōgan era|ja|貞観}} 16), it received the lower fifth Rank in the system of {{ill|Shinkai|ja|神階}}. The main deity is regarded as the god of homes and construction. The shrine was designated a {{ill|Gōsha|ja|郷社}} under the old shrine Ranking system.

== Deities ==
The shrine enshrines the following deities:
* {{ill|Otonoji and Otonobe|ja|大苫辺尊|lt=Otomabe no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Toshigami|ja|大歳神|lt=Otoshi no Kami}}
* {{ill|Wakatakehiko|ja|稚武彦命|lt=Wakatakehiko no Mikoto}}

== Crest ==
* The shrine's crest is a circle with five-seven paulownia (''maru-ni-go-shichi-kiri'').

== Rituals ==
* festival - {{ill|November 3|ja|11月3日}}
* Prayers for the Year - {{ill|Lunisolar February 1|ja|Lunisolar February1日}}
* Summer Festival - {{ill|July 15|ja|7月15日}}
* {{ill|Shinto Dance|ja|神踊り}} - {{ill|August 15|ja|8月15日}}
: Designated as a Tokushima Prefecture Intangible Folk Cultural Property.<ref>[http://www.city.tokushima.tokushima.jp/shakai_kyoiku/gaiyo09.html "Protection and Use of Cultural Properties" (Tokushima City website, cultural property list)]</ref> This festival, originating in the late {{ill|Heian period|ja|平安時代}}, prays for agricultural prosperity and the prevention of epidemics. There are 12 traditional dance songs, each with simple lyrics.
* New Grain Thanksgiving Festival - {{ill|December 23|ja|12月23日}}

== Cultural Properties ==
* {{ill|Kamiyo moji|ja|神代文字}} woodblocks
* {{ill|Hachisuka Mochiaki|ja|蜂須賀茂韶}}'s deity plaque

== Access ==
* From {{ill|Tokushima Station|ja|徳島駅}} (JR), take the Tokushima City Bus to the "Kamiyachiman Elementary School" stop; the shrine is a short walk from there.

{{nihongo|'''Enomiya Shrine'''|宅宮神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}, {{ill|Tokushima (city)|Q207309|qid=Q207309}}, {{ill|Kamihachiman-chō|Q11358489|qid=Q11358489}}. {{nihongo|'''Enomiya Shrine'''|宅宮神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== History ==
The year of establishment is unknown. It is identified with “'''Ōtomahime Shrine''' (おおとまひめじんじゃ)” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} for {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}}, {{ill|Nakata district|Q3205778|qid=Q3205778}} ({{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}).

It is the only shrine among the Shikinaisha that enshrines Ōtomabe no Mikoto. It was ranked first among the twelve shrines of Myōgata District and is a distinguished shrine. In {{ill|874|Q23843|qid=Q23843}} (the 16th year of {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}}), it was granted the court rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}}). The principal deity is said to be a god of households and construction. It was formerly a Gōsha (village shrine).

== Enshrined deities ==
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōtomabe no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Toshigami}}
* {{ill|Wakatakehiko|Q11596350|qid=Q11596350}}

== Shrine crest ==
* Paulownia crest with five-seven arrangement inside a circle

== Festivals and rituals ==
* Annual festival – {{ill|November 3|Q2995|qid=Q2995}}
* Kinen-sai (prayer for a good harvest) – {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Lunar calendar February 1}}
* Summer festival – {{ill|July 15|Q2686|qid=Q2686}}
* Sacred dance – {{ill|August 15|Q2774|qid=Q2774}}
:Designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property of Tokushima Prefecture<ref>[http://www.city.tokushima.tokushima.jp/shakai_kyoiku/gaiyo09.html “Protection and Utilization of Cultural Properties” (Tokushima City website, with links to a list of cultural properties located in the city)]</ref>. Said to have begun in the late {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, this festival is held to pray for “bountiful harvests and the prevention of epidemics.” There are twelve types of dance songs, all with simple lyrics.
* New Harvest Thanksgiving Festival – {{ill|December 23|Q2676|qid=Q2676}}

== Cultural properties ==
* Woodblocks of {{ill|Jindai moji|Q1141193|qid=Q1141193}}
* Shrine name plaque of Lord {{ill|Hachisuka Mochiaki|Q656008|qid=Q656008}}

== Access ==
* From {{ill|Shikoku Railway Company|Q496531|qid=Q496531|lt=JR}} {{ill|Tokushima Station|Q860775|qid=Q860775}}, take the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tokushima City Bus}} and get off at “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kamihachiman Elementary School}}” stop; the shrine is immediately nearby.
